chapter: Postwar records, Miami and Los Angeles
title: Sightseeing, Desi Arnaz's studio and Los Angeles Latin bands
summary: Machito toured Hollywood with Desi Arnaz and notes Eddie Cano's commercial combo as the other Latin band.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: So, all right, but in the Club Brazil did you only had to work at night or did you have matinees?
No, we just worked at night.
What did you do during the daytime?
The daytime, we just go all around to ....
Yeah, sightseeing. I went to Hollywood. In that particular time, Desi Arnaz was making Cuban Pete and he invite me to the studio and he give me a sightseeing to the studio. He was very nice to me.
Okay. At that time, Macho, were there any other Latin bands in California, that were popular, playing Afro-Cuban music?
No, there was a different style; like here
they call it commercial. the name of that pianist, a Mexican pianist, What's very good, and .....?
No, Rene Touzet came later. Gee, I forgot the name of the fellow. A good pianist, in Noro Morales band.
Eddie Cano. He had a combination bass, timbales, a vocalist, and a bongo player and about five or six pieces; but very good.
